claims.text: The signature and essentially only food dish is wheat noodle tsukemen; wheat is present in the kitchen, so any gluten-free request cannot be considered safe.
Whether seasonings or any soy sauce in the broth are wheat-free is not stated; wheat is listed as an allergen for the tsukemen.

The entire menu is vegan with no animal ingredients, so risk of cross-contact with meat, fish, dairy or egg is effectively eliminated. The broth uses donko (dried shiitake) and kombu dashi with soy milk, not fish dashi.
Fully vegan kitchen, so vegan diners do not need to worry about hidden animal ingredients or shared meat/fish surfaces.
Plant-based broth using shiitake and kombu dashi instead of fish/bonito dashi.

The directory listing advises customers to tell staff about their vegetarian/vegan needs and any allergies and to choose a menu item accordingly, implying ordering decisions should be confirmed with staff at the venue.
No soy sauce details published; standard sushi-shop shoyu generally contains wheat. Assume wheat-containing soy sauce unless confirmed otherwise.
This is a seafood-focused sushi kitchen; vegan rolls (cucumber, plum-shiso) are prepared in a space that primarily handles raw fish, so cross-contact with fish is likely.
A couple of genuinely plant-based maki are on the menu: cucumber roll (¥900) and plum-shiso roll (¥900).

No allergen or cross-contamination information is published anywhere. The kitchen prepares wheat-heavy items (baked cakes, sandwiches, curry roux) alongside all other dishes, making cross-contact highly probable.
No tamari or gluten-free soy sauce mentioned. Standard wheat-containing soy sauce is assumed given the menu style (taco rice seasoning, curry, stewed dishes).
Meat and dairy are used throughout the kitchen in multiple dishes simultaneously; no vegan-safe prep area or labeling exists.

No allergy-handling policy is documented on any source. The cafe is a small owner-operated establishment where the single owner/cook handles all preparation; direct inquiry by phone (026-232-7863) before visiting is the only way to assess safety.
Small, owner-run kitchen means fewer hands and potentially more flexibility to accommodate requests — calling ahead in Japanese gives the best chance of a custom accommodation.
No GF items exist; the entire menu is wheat-based. Cross-contamination risk is high by default in a small kitchen producing wheat-flour cakes, tarts, and quiches.
All items contain dairy (butter, cream, cheese). No plant-based preparation space exists.
No allergen handling policies or staff training information is mentioned in any available source. The shop has no menu labeling for allergens.

name: 平五郎 本店 (Patisserie HEIGORO Honten)

claims.text: All shaved ice items list wheat as an allergen; the kitchen works with wheat-containing baked goods throughout. No mention of dedicated preparation areas.
Not a savoury establishment; soy sauce is not used. However wheat is a declared allergen across all shaved ice menu items.
Eggs and dairy are core to all items; no vegan-safe preparation lines exist.
Allergen information is published per item on the website (milk, eggs, wheat, almonds, soy noted for shaved ice); no information is available about how staff handle allergy requests in person.

name: らぁめん みそ家 (Ramen Misoya)

claims.text: Miso and the tare are wheat-containing; ramen noodles are wheat. Assume gluten throughout.
Soba tsuyu is built on wheat-containing soy sauce; buckwheat noodles are often cut with wheat flour (nihachi). Request jūwari + wheat-free tsuyu.
